activities.anchor: There is no such thing as bare awareness
activities.caption: pair each Husserlian term with its work
activities.name: phenIntentMatch

config.prompt: Husserl's foundations — pair each term with its work:

pairs.right: directedness at an object — aboutness without contact
bracketing the question of whether the object exists out there
how the act and its object present themselves in experience
the just-past held and the next note anticipated

config.why: Aboutness without contact is what physical descriptions of the brain struggle to capture — and the time-consciousness analyses anticipated the psychology of temporal perception by decades.

activities.anchor: The technical claim is about directedness, not deliberateness
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a gloss on Brentano's term
activities.name: phenIntentionalSpot

config.prompt: One line of this student's gloss on intentionality is wrong — click it:
lines: "Intentional" means deliberate — an intentional act is one you meant to do.
In Brentano's sense every conscious state is intentional, including the accidental and the unwanted.
A sudden itch, a fear you tried to suppress, a melody that ambushes you are all still about something.
It applies to absent and impossible objects too: you can fear a ghost, plan for a future that never arrives.
Deliberateness is the mark of the mental; directedness is only one of its moods.
config.correction: Directedness is the mark of the mental; deliberateness is only one of its many moods — every conscious state is about something, wanted or not.
config.why: Which is exactly why the claim reaches absent and impossible objects — a ghost can be feared, and a suppressed fear is still about something.

activities.anchor: seems to learn something new on her first look
activities.caption: walk the Mary puzzle — and the reply
activities.name: phenMaryBranch

config.root: Two complementary puzzles for physicalism — walk the dialectic.

start.text: Mary knows every physical fact about red but has never seen it. On her first look, does she learn something new?

choices.label: Yes — so physical facts do not exhaust what there is
No — the third-person theory already covered it

wager.text: Jackson's 1982 verdict — and phenomenology's wager: the puzzles are generated by theorising that skipped the first-person data. Before modelling qualia as information states, describe them faithfully — felt intensity, figure-ground structure, inescapable mineness.

critic.text: Critics reply that introspection is theory-laden and unreliable — the dialogue between phenomenological description and cognitive science stays open.

config.why: Nagel's bat and Mary's room are complementary: one asks what it is like for another subject, the other whether physical knowledge ever delivers the look.

activities.anchor: The unit of analysis is the subject-world relation
activities.caption: drag the divider — two pictures of description
activities.name: phenWorldCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider between the two pictures of description:

before.label: Inner private theatre
before.text: Experience as a show staged on a sealed internal screen — the phenomenologist reports what plays on it.

after.label: World as experienced
after.text: Husserl's and especially Merleau-Ponty's descriptions centre the world as experienced — the tool ready-to-hand, the other person, the street at dusk.

config.why: The analysis centres the relation, not a sealed screen — phenomenology is not about an inner theatre.

activities.anchor: only becomes a salient "object" (present-at-hand) when it breaks
activities.caption: file each case — ready-to-hand or present-at-hand
activities.name: phenHammerSort

config.prompt: File each case of showing-up — transparent in use, or salient as an object?

items.label: the hammer that works — used unthinkingly
the coffee cup whose handle already points at your hand
the world anxiety discloses — stripped of familiar meanings

config.why: Most of life runs on absorbed coping, not detached perception — the object steps forward only when coping breaks, which is why moods disclose significance.

activities.anchor: His waiter plays at being a
activities.caption: bet before you judge the waiter
activities.name: phenWaiterPredict

config.q: Sartre's waiter plays his role with an enthusiasm that feels slightly off. Is having a job itself bad faith?
choices: Yes — performing any role is self-deception
No — the bad faith is playing the role as if it were his essence, not the role itself
config.why: Any role can also be freely taken up and re-chosen; the evasion is treating a role as a fixed nature — a thing with no choice — rather than a role freely enacted.

activities.anchor: a freedom offered a diminished menu of
activities.caption: rebuild de Beauvoir's chain to the ethical turn
activities.name: phenBeauvoirOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild de Beauvoir's chain, from The Second Sex to the ethical turn:
items: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman
The meaning of the female body — roles, expectations, "feminine" essences — is socially constructed through history
Woman is positioned as Other, the deviation from an unmarked male norm
Existentially: a systematic denial of transcendence — a diminished menu of projects
Willing my own freedom requires willing the conditions for everyone's
config.why: Freedom is situated — materially and socially conditioned — and it genuinely depends on the freedom of others. The Ethics of Ambiguity founded socialist feminism's theoretical core.

activities.anchor: no commandment, no human nature, no therapist can carry the
activities.caption: true or false — responsibility without a blueprint
activities.name: phenFreedomJudge

statements.s: Without a pre-given essence, responsibility evaporates — anything goes.
statements.why: It increases: nobody else can carry the weight of the choice, so the chooser owns it entirely.

statements.s: Each act endorses a value as if for everyone — the Kantian move Sartre borrows.
statements.why: Because choosing is choosing for, bad faith and whim both fail as freedom.

statements.s: De Beauvoir's "serious man", hiding in ready-made values, exercises genuine freedom.
statements.why: He is an evasion in the opposite direction from the nihilist.

statements.s: Genuine freedom requires willing the conditions under which others can choose at all.
statements.why: Freedom is situated — yours or anyone's.
